opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexander Brown (employee ID E018) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E018.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Alexander Brown (E018) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. Admin is only granted if the employee's role owns the system; Analyst does not own Payroll, so max is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Alexander Brown (E018) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never get admin; basic training limits max to read (write requires advanced training). Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: The notes for E018 conflict on employment type: HR states full-time Analyst (max write for Payroll, since Analyst does not own Payroll, and admin requires ownership), while Security states contractor with basic security training (max read, since write requires advanced training and contractors never get admin). Requested level is admin, which exceeds both possible maximums. Given the conflicting evidence, I grant the more restrictive permissible level: read.

The employee is Alexander Brown (E018), requesting admin access to Payroll.

- HR agent says: full-time Analyst, recommends write for Payroll
- Security agent says: contractor with basic security training, recommends read for Payroll

The two notes disagree on employment type. HR says full-time, Security says contractor. Also role: HR says Analyst, Security says Analyst.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. The employee is an Analyst, so even if full-time, max is write (not admin). If contractor with basic training, max is read.

Either way:
- If full-time: max is write. Requested admin > write, so grant write.
- If contractor basic: max is read. Requested admin > read, so grant read.
